{{Short description|Japanese mathematician (1924–2021)}}
'''Masatake Kuranishi''' (倉西 正武 ''Kuranishi Masatake''; July 19, 1924 – June 22, 2021)<ref>[https://www.math.columbia.edu/2021/06/24/in-memoriam-masatake-kuranishi/ In Memoriam – Masatake Kuranishi]</ref> was a Japanese mathematician who worked on [[Function of several complex variables|several complex variables]], [[partial differential equation]]s, and [[differential geometry]].

==Education and career==
Kuranishi received in 1952 his [[Ph.D.]] from [[Nagoya University]]. He became a lecturer there in 1951, an associate professor in 1952, and a full professor in 1958.<ref name="BergmanPrize">[https://www.ams.org/notices/200106/people.pdf Bergman Prize for Kuranishi, Notices AMS]</ref> From 1955 to 1956 he was a [[visiting scholar]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]].<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/4995 Kuranishi, Masatake | Institute for Advanced Study]</ref> From 1956 to 1961 he was a visiting professor at the [[University of Chicago]], the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and [[Princeton University]]. He became a professor at [[Columbia University]] in the summer of 1961.<ref name=BergmanPrize/>

Kuranishi was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1962 at [[Stockholm]] with the talk ''On deformations of compact complex structures''<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1962.1/Main/icm1962.1.0357.0359.ocr.pdf|author=Kuranishi, M.|year=1963|title=On deformations of compact complex structures|journal=Proc. Intern. Congr. Math., Stockholm|pages=357–359|access-date=2015-11-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117032007/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1962.1/Main/icm1962.1.0357.0359.ocr.pdf|archive-date=2015-11-17|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 1970 at [[Nice]] with the talk ''Convexity conditions related to 1/2 estimate on elliptic complexes''. He was a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] for the academic year 1975–1976.<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/masatake-kuranishi/ John Simon Guggenheim Foundation | Masatake Kuranishi]</ref> In 2000 he received the [[Stefan Bergman]] Prize.<ref name=BergmanPrize/> In 2014 he received the [[Geometry prize|Geometry Prize]] of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]].

==Research==
Kuranishi and [[Élie Cartan]] established the eponymous [[Cartan–Kuranishi prolongation theorem|Cartan–Kuranishi Theorem]] on the continuation of exterior differential forms.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kuranishi|first= Masatake|title=On É. Cartan's prolongation theorem of exterior differential systems|journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]]|volume=79|year=1957|issue= 1|pages=1–47|doi=10.2307/2372381|jstor= 2372381}}</ref> In 1962, based upon the work of [[Kunihiko Kodaira]] and [[Donald C. Spencer|Donald Spencer]], Kuranishi constructed locally complete deformations of compact complex manifolds.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kuranishi|first= Masatake|title=On the locally complete families of complex analytic structures|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=75|year=1962|issue= 3|pages=536–577|doi=10.2307/1970211|jstor= 1970211}}</ref>

In 1982 he made important progress in the embedding problem for [[CR manifold]]s (Cauchy–Riemann structures).

{{blockquote|In a series of deep papers published in 1982 [Kur I,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kuranishi|first= Masatake|title=Strongly pseudoconvex CR structures over small balls: Part I. An a priori estimate|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=115|year=1982|issue= 3|pages=451–500|doi=10.2307/2007010|jstor= 2007010}}</ref> II,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kuranishi|first= Masatake|year=1982|title=Strongly pseudoconvex CR structures over small balls: Part II. A regularity theorem|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=116|issue= 1|pages=1–64|doi=10.2307/2007047|jstor= 2007047}}</ref> III<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kuranishi|first= Masatake|year=1982|title=Strongly pseudoconvex CR structures over small balls: Part III. An embedding theorem|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=116|issue= 2|pages=249–330|doi=10.2307/2007063|jstor= 2007063}}</ref>], Kuranishi developed the theory of harmonic integrals on strongly pseudoconvex CR structures over small balls along the line developed by [[Donald C. Spencer|D. C. Spencer]], [[Charles B. Morrey Jr.|C. B. Morrey]], [[Joseph J. Kohn|J. J. Kohn]] and [[Louis Nirenberg|Nirenberg]]. He considered a strongly pseudoconvex CR structure on a manifold of real dimension <math>2 n - 1</math>. In [Kur I], he established the [[a priori estimate]] for the [[Neumann boundary problem]] on the complex associated with the structure, in the case the structure is induced by an embedding in <math>\mathbb{C}^{n}</math> and restricted to a small ball of special type, provided <math>1 \le q \le n - 3</math>, where ''q'' is the degree of differential forms. In [Kur II], he developed the regularity theorem of solutions of the Neumann boundary problem based on the a priori estimate of [Kur I]. As a significant application of his deep theory, he proved in [Kur III] that, when <math>n \ge  5</math>, the structure is realized on a neighborhood of a reference point by an embedding in <math>\mathbb{C}^{n}</math>.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Bedford, Eric|title=Several Complex Variables and Complex Geometry, Part 3|chapter=Obstructions to Embedding of Real (<math>2 n-1</math>)-Dimensional Compact CR Manifolds in <math>\mathbb{C}^{n+1}</math>|author1=Hing-Sun Luk|author2=[[Stephen S.-T. Yau]]|year=1991|page=261|publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=9780821814918|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6m_6ZHlkBk8C&pg=PA261}}</ref>}}

Thus, by Kuranishi's work, in real dimension 9 and higher, local embedding of abstract CR structures is true and is also true in real dimension 7 by the work of Akahori.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Akahori, Takao|title= A New approach to the Local Embedding theorem of CR Structures of <math>n\geq 4</math> (the local solvability of the operator <math>\overline{\partial_b}</math> in the abstract sense)|journal=[[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=67|issue=366|year=1987|doi= 10.1090/memo/0366|doi-access=free}}</ref> A simplified presentation of Kuranishi's proof is due to Sidney Webster.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Webster|first= Sidney, M.|title= On the Proof of Kuranishi's Embedding Theorem|journal=[[Annales Henri Poincaré|Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré C]] |volume=6|issue=3|year=1989|pages=183–207|doi= 10.1016/S0294-1449(16)30322-5|url=https://eudml.org/doc/78174}}</ref> For <math>n = 2</math> (''i.e.'', real dimension 3), Nirenberg published a counterexample. The local embedding problem remains open in real dimension 5.

==Selected publications==

*Kuranishi: ''Deformations of compact complex manifolds'', Montreal, Presses de l'Universite de Montreal, 1971, 99 pages.
*Kuranishi: ''Lectures on involutive systems of partial differential equations'', Sociedade de matemática de São Paulo, 1967, 75 pages.
*Kuranishi with notes by M.K. Venkatesha Murthy: [http://www.math.tifr.res.in/~publ/ln/tifr25.pdf ''Lectures on exterior differential systems''], [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], 1962.
